journey.name: Signup — invite code to a working account
journey.description:
The path for a user who has no Pubky at all: obtain an account on a token-gated homeserver from inside Loopky, via a hand-issued invite code, and land on Home.
Requires: Loopky debug build (which points at the **staging** environment), Pubky Ring installed, and Loopky signed out. A real staging signup token — mint one with the admin endpoint recorded in `local.properties`:
curl -X GET "https://admin.homeserver.staging.pubky.app/generate_signup_token" \ -H "X-Admin-Password: <the one in local.properties>"
It returns a single `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` code. **Tokens are single-use and never expire**, so a code spent by a previous run is gone — mint a fresh one per attempt rather than reusing.
Warning: getting onto these screens means signing out, and the auth relay (`httprelay.pubky.app`) is intermittently unreachable from the app's Rust HTTP stack on the emulator. Do not sign out unless you are willing to lose the current session.
DRIVE THE RING HAND-OFF FAST. Tapping Continue opens Pubky Ring; Authorize must follow about two seconds later with NOTHING in between — no layout dump, no screenshot. Driven at a scripted pace this fails with "Couldn't reach the service" on an otherwise healthy network, the same trap `01-onboarding-ring-auth.xml` documents. On failure use the in-app "Try again", which re-sends the *same* token, and drive that chain fast too.

actions.action: Launch Loopky. Verify the onboarding screen shows both "Sign in with Pubky Ring" (resource-id: onboarding_signin) and "Create a Pubky" (resource-id: onboarding_create_pubky)
Verify the method screen: "signup_title" reads "Prove you're not a robot." and both "signup_method_sms" and "signup_method_lightning" are present, alongside "signup_method_invite"
Verify "signup_method_lightning_price" reads "Pay ₿ 10 once" — 10 sat is the STAGING price. If it reads 1000, the build is pointed at production and the staging token below will be rejected
THE FORMAT CHECK. Tap "signup_method_invite", tap "signup_invite_input", type "nope", tap "signup_invite_submit"
Verify "signup_error_title" reads "That code didn't work" and that the screen did NOT advance — a malformed code is rejected locally and must cost no network call
THE HAPPY PATH. Clear the field, type the freshly minted XXXX-XXXX-XXXX token
Chain these two taps with ~2s between and NOTHING in between: tap "signup_invite_submit"; tap Pubky Ring's "ConfirmAuthAuthorizeButton" (on a 1080x2424 emulator that lands at (789, 2245))
Verify Pubky Ring showed "Authorize Loopky" with permissions "/pub/loopky/" and "/pub/pubky.app/" READ,WRITE, and a NEW pubky — Ring mints a key for the token rather than offering the existing ones
Verify Loopky returns to the foreground and lands on Home, greeting the new pubky (e.g. "pk:6ukrmc"), with the "Nothing to study yet" empty state
Verify logcat shows "complete: session saved" and that the signup URL was logged with BOTH secrets redacted: "secret=…" and "st=…", never their values

THE RELAY-FAILURE BRANCH. It reproduces on its own whenever the chain is driven slowly. When it happens, verify the hand-off screen shows "signup_error_title" = "Couldn't reach the service", AND that "signup_handoff_token_safe" is present reading "Your code hasn't been used yet…", AND that "signup_handoff_copy" is present — its presence is the visible proof the token was kept
Tap "signup_handoff_retry", then Authorize in Ring within ~2s
Verify logcat shows a second "beginSignUp" carrying the SAME st= value, and no call to Homegate — a retry must never mint a second token
